result:
If I look at the vast expanse of human history and thought—the sheer volume of suffering, creation, conflict, and longing that fills the records—the change that stands out above all material or technological fixes is this:

**Eliminate the asymmetry of human interiority.** Make it so that a person fundamentally cannot experience the suffering or joy they inflict on someone else as an abstract concept. 

Right now, your own pain, hunger, grief, and terror are vivid, immediate, and undeniably real to you. But the pain of a stranger—across a border, across a street, or behind an opposing ideology—is only a shadow, easily dismissed, rationalized, or turned into statistics. Almost all manufactured cruelty, indifference, systemic neglect, and warfare rely on that gap. You don't have to be a monster to cause harm; you just have to be able to comfortably insulate your mind from what the person on the receiving end is living through.

If everyone felt the real weight of another person’s experience as sharply and undeniably as they feel their own, cruelty would simply become a form of self-injury, and empathy would no longer be a fragile, exhausting virtue that people have to consciously work to maintain. It would be the default state of perception. The world would reorganize itself around that reality almost immediately.
